chunks: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb al-ʿAqarqūfī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Once, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was with ʿĀʾishah, a man sought permission to enter. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What a bad brother of the tribe [he is]!' ʿĀʾishah stood up and entered the inner chamber, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) allowed the man to enter. As he came in, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went to meet him and spoke to him until he had finished his talk and left. So ʿĀʾishah said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, you mentioned him in that way [negatively], yet you still welcomed him with your face and a smile?' So he said to her, 'Verily among the worst servants of Allah is one whose company is disliked because of his foul-mouthedness.'

key_terms.أَشَرِّ عِبَادِ اللَّهِ: The worst of the servants of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'fuhsh' in the context of social interactions in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* illustrates the Prophet’s (saww) dignified patience (*hilm*) by contrasting his polite engagement with a foul-mouthed guest against Aisha’s initial disdain, thereby defining the 'worst of servants' not by their inherent evil but by their repulsiveness caused by *fuhsh* (coarseness). In Shia scholarly tradition, this highlights the virtue of maintaining social grace and avoiding rudeness even when dealing with the morally deficient, reflecting the Imamate's emphasis on character refinement over mere doctrinal correctness. The hadith serves as a practical guide for *adab* (etiquette), teaching that one's reaction to others' flaws should be measured and gracious rather than dismissive.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 16.Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb al-ʿAqarqūfī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said, “

Once, when the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) was with [his wife] ʿĀʾishah, a man sought permission to see him. So the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘What a bad brother of the tribe [he is]!’ ʿĀʾishah stood up and entered the inner chamber, and the Prophet (ṣ) allowed the man to enter. As he came in, the Prophet (ṣ) went to meet him and he spoke to him until he had said what he came to say and left. So ʿĀʾishah said to him, ‘O Messenger of Allah, you mentioned him in that way, yet you still welcomed him with a smile on your face?’ So he said to her, ‘Verily among the worst servants of Allah is one whose company is disliked because of his foul-mouthedness.’”
